items.title: Frank Tiberi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 30, 2022

ctx.x: So I’m looking at the pop hits from ’47, around that time you have people like Ted Weems and Sammy Kaye — I mean you even have the “Too Fat Polka” by Arthur Godfrey. So my question is, if you can recall what your song list — what was the repertoire like back then?

Oh that’s pretty hard, really hard actually. But I mean the only thing I can remember is just a few things such as Frank Rossolino was my roommate and of course what Bob Chester did was you know his wife owned the Fisher Body Company and he was just like

carried along like rattled through. And every time that he wanted to play the saxophone he would stop and call the guy, which would be me, to come up and do the solo. But he was joking all around actually. He was just riding around with a Town and Country car and as I say, he was just, you know, he wasn’t playing at all. But he did own a saxophone.
